node_types.name: Service
node_types.definition: A deployable runtime component that handles requests, performs work, or coordinates other components

node_types.name: Store
node_types.definition: A persistent data store that holds state across requests and process lifetimes

node_types.name: ChainPool
node_types.definition: A managed pool of external blockchain node replicas exposing the chain's native protocol (JSON-RPC, chain-sync, mini-protocols, etc.); the pool is the source of truth for its chain. Replicas may have mixed roles (archive vs pruned-tip) and mixed client implementations for byzantine cross-checking. The pool is partitioned by (chain_id, fork_id) into fork sub-pools, supports per-replica drain state under the pool-drain protocol, reports tip-lag for tip-staleness detection, and exposes mTLS surfaces enumerated in cert-inventory.

node_types.name: Client
node_types.definition: An external API consumer (developer's application) that calls the gateway over HTTP or WebSocket

nodes.definition: Stateless authenticated request entry: validates API keys, residency policy, and tenant_cluster identity / suspension state against auth_cache (with tenant_store as the canonical source on miss); requires every inbound request to carry a current valid edge-attestation (signed by edge) and rejects any request that does not, regardless of source IP or apparent network position; legitimately edge-bypassing traffic (health checks, control plane, region_coordinator → gateway) carries an explicit internal-identity attestation, never an implicit network-position trust. As a residency-policy consumer, gateway pins the residency policy_version it enforced on every outgoing request (to chain_router, fanout, usage_meter), and cross-checks the policy_version carried in the inbound edge-attestation so downstream mismatch is detectable; subscribes to region_coordinator's residency_publisher push-and-acknowledge channel and must acknowledge readiness within the documented window before residency_publisher activates a tightening change; if gateway fails to acknowledge in-window it falls to deny-by-default for the affected tenant rather than serve under the old version past activation. Enforces per-key and per-cluster rate limits via auth_cache and global throttle flags pushed by region_coordinator (cluster-level throttle and suspension flags propagate the same fast-path as per-tenant flags). Records usage with usage_meter, tagging rejected-request signals with rejection reason (rate-limit, throttle, residency, revoked, malformed-auth, plan-change-overage, cluster-suspended, tenant-offboarded). Routes RPC requests to chain_router and websocket subscriptions to fanout, threading an explicit (chain, fork) tag derived from the request so chain_router and fanout serve the requested fork; tip-state RPC responses are annotated with the answering pool's freshness state when the pool is in tip-stale mode. Classifies TLS / mTLS handshake errors against chain_router and chain pool as a distinct error class from upstream-chain network errors so on-call signal points at the right surface. Enforces a free-tier trust ramp: capacity (concurrent subscriptions, cost class access, mempool stream access, address_index watch counts) unlocks gradually as verified-attribute signals accrue (validated payment instrument, captcha, domain ownership, age-of-tenant, cluster reputation). Plan downgrades are graceful: existing in-flight subscriptions and long-RPC slots that exceed new caps are not killed; new requests over the new caps are rejected with a 'plan-change-overage' reason. On tenant offboarding, closes all open websocket subscriptions for the tenant with a structured 'tenant-offboarded' close reason, deduping inbound offboarding signals from region_coordinator by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meeting a documented attestation SLO and surfacing preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when a subscription cannot be torn down because it overlaps a preservation hold) so region_coordinator can record a best-effort attestation rather than waiting indefinitely on timeout. Time-bucketed enforcement uses the hybrid logical clock from region_coordinator rather than wall-clock; observed inter-region clock skew above a threshold transitions the region into a documented degraded mode. Deployed in every region; no per-connection state outside auth_cache and fanout

Ethereum mainnet chain-node pool: a managed group of replicas with mixed roles — archive replicas (historical state, served on the historical-isolated path) and pruned tip replicas (current-state reads), preferably across diverse client implementations (Erigon + Geth) for byzantine cross-checking; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool. Replicas declare their (chain_id, fork_id) allegiance so chain_router partitions the pool by fork sub-pool. Replicas support an explicit drain state under chain_router's pool-drain protocol, finishing in-flight RPCs and unsubscribing from fanout head streams only after gateway-side subscriptions have re-bound. Each replica reports tip-lag relative to chain peer count / expected slot advance so chain_router can mark the pool tip-stale when it falls behind the per-chain freshness budget. mTLS surface to chain_router and fanout is enumerated in cert-inventory

Sepolia testnet chain-node pool: a managed group of replicas mirroring the Ethereum pool's role split (archive + pruned tip), serving Sepolia's RPC and chain-sync interfaces; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool. Replicas declare their (chain_id, fork_id) allegiance so chain_router partitions the pool by fork sub-pool. Replicas support an explicit drain state under chain_router's pool-drain protocol. Each replica reports tip-lag against chain peer count / expected slot advance for tip-staleness detection. mTLS surface to chain_router and fanout is enumerated in cert-inventory

Bitcoin chain-node pool: multiple Bitcoin Core replicas with txindex (archive role) plus pruned tip replicas, ZMQ notifications surfaced as chain-sync streams; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool. Replicas declare their (chain_id, fork_id) allegiance so chain_router partitions the pool by fork sub-pool. Replicas support an explicit drain state under chain_router's pool-drain protocol. Each replica reports tip-lag relative to chain peer count / expected block advance for tip-staleness detection. mTLS surface to chain_router and fanout is enumerated in cert-inventory

Cardano chain-node pool: multiple Cardano-node + Ogmios bridge replicas (archive + pruned tip roles), exposing chain-sync, local-state-query, and local-tx-monitor; chain_router and fanout select replicas from the pool. Replicas declare their (chain_id, fork_id) allegiance so chain_router partitions the pool by fork sub-pool. Replicas support an explicit drain state under chain_router's pool-drain protocol. Each replica reports tip-lag relative to chain peer count / expected slot advance for tip-staleness detection. mTLS surface to chain_router and fanout is enumerated in cert-inventory

Canonical multi-region store of tenants, API keys, plan tiers, tenant_cluster identity, residency policy, preservation holds, erasure tombstones, and rate-limit / quota state. Partitioned by tenant residency policy (residency-scoped, not globally replicated for residency-pinned tenants). Concurrent writes resolve under an explicit policy: per-key single-writer in the tenant's home region for adds/updates, with global tombstoned revocations that any region observes regardless of replication direction (tombstones are not subject to last-write-wins). Plan-change events (upgrade, downgrade, suspension) are stored and propagated as globally-ordered tombstones with an effective-from timestamp so any region's auth_cache and tenant_store hydration sees a consistent view of which plan is in force at any point in time. Tenant_cluster identity groups tenants by signup metadata, source-network fingerprints, behavioral signals, and query-pattern similarity; cluster assignment evolves as more behavioral signal accrues and cluster-level suspensions are tombstoned and propagate cross-region like key revocations. Preservation orders are recorded as tombstoned hold records keyed on (tenant, data_class, scope, time_range); held data is exempt from retention rotation and erasure of overlapping data is denied while a hold is in force. Tenant erasure requests are durable tombstones that propagate cross-region and produce a per-store deletion attestation aggregated into a verifiable certificate of deletion; preservation-erasure conflicts resolve under a documented preservation-wins policy. Once a tenant is offboarded and its erasure attestation is final, that tenant identity cannot be resurrected — attempts to reuse the id are rejected. Supports a documented 'extract for tenant T' operation returning only T's data, scoped to the residency policy in force, suitable for fulfilling a lawful-access or data-subject-access request without disclosing other tenants. Each region holds the partitions it is allowed to host. Internal channels to gateway, usage_meter, region_coordinator are cert-bearing surfaces enumerated in cert-inventory
External developer application that connects to the gateway over HTTP for request/response RPC and over WebSocket for real-time subscriptions

Public-facing untrusted-traffic filter: terminates TLS, applies IP-level rate limiting, runs WAF / bot-mitigation rules, classifies source-network fingerprint, and forwards only API-key-bearing traffic to the gateway. Mints a short-lived cryptographically signed edge-attestation on every forwarded request that includes the tenant's residency tag, source-network classification, signup-fingerprint signal for the tenant-clustering pipeline, edge-applied rate-limit verdicts, and the pinned residency policy_version under which edge enforced the request; the policy_version travels in the attestation so downstream consumers (gateway, usage_meter, metrics_store) can detect mismatch. As a residency-policy consumer, edge subscribes to region_coordinator's residency_publisher push-and-acknowledge channel: on every published policy update it must acknowledge readiness within the documented window before residency_publisher activates a tightening change; if edge fails to acknowledge in-window it falls to deny-by-default for the affected tenant rather than serve under the old version past activation. gateway rejects any request lacking a current valid attestation regardless of source IP. Edge is enumerated as a cert-bearing surface in the cert-inventory: TLS-termination cert, attestation-signing key, and any mTLS to gateway each have a documented renewal cadence with overlap-window acceptance, rotated under region_coordinator's region-staggered gating. Routing is residency-aware: requests from a residency-pinned tenant (looked up via region_coordinator) are forwarded only to gateways in regions allowed by that tenant's policy, even when an out-of-policy region is closer by anycast. On reconnect storms (anycast flap, region drain), edge advertises jittered-backoff hints and regional affinity hints to clients so reconnect load spreads across surviving regions. Consumes a per-region gateway health surface (sourced via region_coordinator) that aggregates per-Subrole liveness — in particular fanout-suspended versus rpc-healthy — so anycast / residency-aware routing can shift subscription traffic away from a region whose subscription path is degraded even when that region's RPC path is healthy. Deployed at the network edge with anycast routing across regions

Per-chain routing service: receives authenticated RPC requests carrying an explicit (chain, fork) tag, selects a healthy non-draining replica from the matching fork sub-pool of the region's chain pool, enforces per-tenant query cost budgets, isolates heavy historical queries onto the historical-replica subset, observes replica-level chain-head and fork-allegiance signals and reports them to region_coordinator (which computes a quorum-based canonical tip per (chain, fork) across all regions); for high-value reads against tip, requires the canonical tip from region_coordinator rather than treating its region's pool as authoritative. Every head observation submitted to region_coordinator's tip_quorum is tagged with the authenticated source replica identity of the submitting chain_router replica, signed over the cert-bearing inter-region surface (mTLS to region_coordinator), so region_coordinator's tip_quorum can attribute each observation to a specific chain_router replica and apply per-source rate limiting and adversarial-source quarantine. Canonicalizes every JSON-RPC response leaving a chain pool against a per-(chain, method, schema_version) schema before forwarding to gateway: undocumented optional fields stripped or sorted, types coerced, intra-response ordering rules applied so response shape is independent of which client implementation answered. Quarantines replicas whose canonicalized response shape diverges from pool consensus the same way it quarantines tip-divergent replicas; partitions a chain pool by replica fork allegiance so cross-fork divergence is sub-pool membership, not quarantine. Detects unannounced consensus splits (replicas in a pool diverging into two stable subgroups, neither a transient reorg) and emits a 'fork-detected' alert with a documented operator-decision SLA before the split becomes user-visible. Measures each pool's tip lag against an out-of-band reference (peer-regional pools via region_coordinator, plus chain peer count / expected slot advance) and marks pools 'tip-stale' when they exceed a per-chain freshness budget; tip-stale pools are excluded from canonical-tip quorum and gateway annotates responses they answer. Exposes an explicit pool-drain protocol: a replica entering 'draining' state stops receiving new requests, finishes in-flight RPCs (or returns them with a retryable-on-other-replica hint), and only after gateway has re-bound any dependent subscriptions does the replica unsubscribe from fanout's head streams. Schema-skew and tip-divergence quarantines consult region_coordinator's 'rotation in progress' tag and suppress quarantines triggered solely by the documented rotation window. At RPC submission time it returns a per-method cost-class hint (short-RPC vs long-RPC, with expected wall-clock band and resource profile) so callers can partition their in-flight slot pool. Cancels in-flight long-RPCs for offboarded tenants, deduping cancellation signals by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meeting a documented attestation SLO and surfacing preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when an in-flight long-RPC overlaps a preservation hold) so region_coordinator can record best-effort attestations on timeout. Every operator-override admission path inside chain_router (pool_membership_manager safe-membership-floor override for emergency-rollover replica admission, drain_coordinator force-complete, and any analogous override) is gated locally and admitted only when the override proposal carries M-of-N signatures from distinct operator credentials drawn from region_coordinator's published credential roster under the parent-scope operator-credential authorization model; chain_router rejects override proposals whose signing credentials are not currently on the roster, refuses to commit override proposals after a compromise-revocation has invalidated any in-flight signature, records the signing operator identities with each commit for the per-operator audit trail, and consumes credential-roster updates and revocations from region_coordinator ahead of admitting further overrides so a single compromised credential cannot mass-admit attacker-controlled replicas. Cert-bearing surface for mTLS to chain pool replicas and to region_coordinator's tip_quorum, enumerated in cert-inventory

Subscription multiplex layer: maintains the upstream chain-sync / newHeads / mempool subscriptions to each region's chain pools (per (chain, fork) sub-pool), publishes events to fanout_bus which subscriber-handling instances read from, multiplexes events to many client websockets, populates the per-chain address index, and emits explicit rollback notifications on reorg. Cursors are portable: each event is tagged with both an opaque cursor and a globally-meaningful chain coordinate (block number + intra-block index, or chain-stream sequence) so any region can replay from the cursor by reconstructing from the chain pool's history when its local ring buffer does not cover that coordinate. Canonical-tip and rollback decisions come from region_coordinator (per (chain, fork)) so subscribers reconnecting across regions see one canonical timeline per fork. Event ordering exposed to subscribers uses chain-derived sequencing rather than wall-clock; the hybrid logical clock from region_coordinator is used only when chain ordering does not apply (e.g. cross-chain bookkeeping). Distinguishes a planned head-stream rebind (driven by chain pool rotation, signalled by chain_router's drain protocol) from a network fault: subscription cursors and consumer-rate state are preserved through a rebind and only a single 'rebind' event surfaces to subscribers, never a spurious rollback. Mempool / pending-transaction subscription delivery has an explicit fairness model: per-event delivery order across subscribers is derived from a deterministic shuffling keyed on (event_id, subscription_id) with a fixed delay budget bounding best-vs-worst delivery skew; no internal, admin, co-located, or commercially-favoured subscriber receives mempool events on a faster path; consumer-rate feedback is advisory only for mempool streams. Head-event and watched-address subscriptions emit a periodic progress heartbeat carrying the answering pool's last-observed-tip and freshness state so a silent subscription is distinguishable from a healthy chain quiet period vs a stalled pool. Exposes a per-subscription consumer-rate feedback signal (lag, dropped-event count, queue depth) so callers can implement bounded per-subscription backpressure and slow-consumer overflow policy on non-mempool streams, and accepts batched subscribe calls (multiple subscriptions per RPC) so reconnect-storm subscribe load can be coalesced. On tenant offboarding, drops the tenant's subscriptions and emits a single accounting record; dedupes inbound offboarding signals from region_coordinator by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meets a documented attestation SLO, and surfaces preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when a subscription's accounting record cannot be finalized because it overlaps a preservation hold) so region_coordinator can record a best-effort attestation rather than waiting indefinitely on timeout. Cert-bearing surface for mTLS to gateway and chain pool replicas, enumerated in cert-inventory

Per-chain index of recent block events keyed by address; populated by the fanout layer from each chain's block stream and read on every new block to match address-activity subscribers without scanning all subscriber filters. Watch entries are claim-stamped per tenant: when a tenant offboards, only that tenant's claim on a watched address is removed (recorded as a per-tenant tombstone), never a hard delete of the underlying watch row when other tenants share it. Dedupes inbound offboarding signals from region_coordinator by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meets a documented attestation SLO, and surfaces preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when a tenant's watch claim overlaps an active preservation hold and cannot be tombstoned-and-rotated) so region_coordinator can record a best-effort attestation rather than waiting indefinitely on timeout. Supports a 'extract for tenant T' operation returning only T's watch claims for compliance fulfilment

Per-region cache of tenant credentials, plan tier (and current plan_version), tenant_cluster identity, residency policy (with the pinned policy_version under which each cached entry was hydrated), and rolling rate-limit / quota counters. Hydrated from tenant_store on miss, but tombstoned signals from region_coordinator — per-tenant throttle flags, plan-change tombstones, cluster-level throttle flags, cluster suspensions, key revocations, and erasure tombstones — take precedence over and propagate ahead of fine-grained counter replication via the same fast-path. Supports deny-during-propagation pending markers on the unified fast-path: when flag_propagator publishes a pending-marker for a high-severity flag (cluster-suspended, key-revocation, erasure-tombstone) before the per-region apply lands, auth_cache treats the pending-marker as deny-by-default for the affected identity until the per-region apply commits and a flag-applied attestation is written back to flag_propagator; reads against a marker-covered identity short-circuit to a documented deny reason rather than serving the prior cached state. Every accepted pending-marker must carry an originating-proposal-id and an HLC expiry bound; auth_cache rejects pending-markers that lack an originating-proposal-id and refuses to install them, so an unattributed marker cannot indefinitely deny traffic. Pending-markers auto-clear when their carried HLC expiry bound is reached without an explicit retraction, so a stalled or rejected proposal cannot leave a stuck deny-by-default state in place; on apply commit, auth_cache reconciles the pending-marker by matching the inbound flag-applied attestation's originating-proposal-id to the installed marker rather than by identity alone, so an apply attestation for a different proposal targeting the same identity does not silently clear an unrelated pending-marker. Throttle flags are stored with an explicit monotonic version per tenant so long-running paths (active websocket subscriptions, streaming or chunked RPC responses) can re-check the flag cheaply by version comparison without re-running the full auth path. Hydration log records auth events per tenant and supports a 'extract for tenant T' operation suitable for compliance use without disclosing other tenants. Supports bulk hydration paths so a reconnect storm into a region does not produce an N-fold tenant_store read amplification. Internal channel to gateway, tenant_store, and region_coordinator's flag_propagator is a cert-bearing surface enumerated in cert-inventory

Per-tenant metering and accounting in each region: records request count, response bytes, chain-node CPU cost, and websocket egress against each API key, tagging every cost record with (tenant, plan_version, tenant_cluster, residency_policy_version) so month-to-date cost is attributable to the plan, cluster, and residency policy in force at the time the cost was incurred. As a residency-policy consumer, usage_meter pins the residency policy_version it enforced on every outgoing record and propagates it to metrics_store / region_coordinator so downstream mismatch is detectable; subscribes to region_coordinator's residency_publisher push-and-acknowledge channel and must acknowledge readiness within the documented window before residency_publisher activates a tightening change; if usage_meter fails to acknowledge in-window it falls to deny-by-default for the affected tenant (rejects new metering writes for that tenant) rather than persist records under the old version past activation. Aggregates cost and rate per tenant_cluster so free-tier and trial-tier global quotas can be enforced at cluster level by region_coordinator's throttle-flag fast-path. Reports deltas to region_coordinator on a sub-second cadence so global cost ceilings and rate limits are enforced against globally-aggregated counters rather than region-local ones; accepts a tagged rejected-request signal from gateway with rejection reason (rate-limit, throttle, residency, revoked, malformed-auth, plan-change-overage, cluster-suspended, tenant-offboarded) so per-tenant cost attribution covers shadow load from rejected requests and key-anomaly detection observes the rejection signal alongside accepted traffic. Detects anomalous per-key behaviour (geo, IP, request-pattern shifts) and surfaces alerts; feeds behavioral and query-pattern signals into the tenant-clustering pipeline. Supports a 'extract for tenant T' operation returning only T's cost records, scoped to the residency policy in force, for compliance fulfilment. Freezes a tenant's cost record at offboarding time so post-offboarding cost cannot accrue; dedupes inbound offboarding signals from region_coordinator by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meets a documented attestation SLO, and surfaces preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when a tenant's cost record overlaps an active preservation hold and cannot be frozen-and-rotated) so region_coordinator can record a best-effort attestation rather than waiting indefinitely on timeout. Internal channels to tenant_store, metrics_store, region_coordinator are cert-bearing surfaces enumerated in cert-inventory

Time-series store of per-tenant usage, error, latency, and rate-limit-headroom metrics with at least 30 days of retention; readable by tenants through the metrics API surfaced on the gateway. Sharded by residency policy: a residency-pinned tenant's metrics are physically located only in regions allowed by their policy. As a residency-policy consumer, metrics_store pins the residency policy_version under which each metric record was admitted (every record carries the policy_version pinned by its writer) and rejects writes whose pinned policy_version does not match its currently-enforced version, so mismatch is detectable end-to-end; subscribes to region_coordinator's residency_publisher push-and-acknowledge channel and must acknowledge readiness within the documented window before residency_publisher activates a tightening change; if metrics_store fails to acknowledge in-window it falls to deny-by-default for the affected tenant (rejects new writes for that tenant) rather than admit records under the old version past activation. Every data class held has an explicit retention policy with a documented minimum (regulatory floor) and maximum (privacy ceiling); retention is enforced as automated rotation, not manual cleanup, and is inspectable per tenant; preservation holds (recorded in tenant_store) exempt held data from rotation. Hosts an immutable, append-only compliance audit trail of all compliance operations (extract, hold-create, hold-release, erasure-request, erasure-attestation, offboarding-attestation) with operator identity captured per operation; the audit trail is itself residency-scoped and retention-managed. Supports a 'extract for tenant T' operation returning only T's metrics scoped to residency policy. Internal channel to usage_meter is a cert-bearing surface enumerated in cert-inventory

Per-region pub/sub multiplex layer that fanout publishes each upstream chain stream to and that subscriber-handling fanout instances read from to deliver to client websockets. Carries its own health, capacity budget, and failover policy. Region-local; cross-region delivery uses the canonical-tip + portable-cursor path on region_coordinator, not bus replication. The bus does not implement subscriber-priority semantics; mempool fairness is enforced at fanout's delivery layer, not by privileged bus consumers

Global control plane for multi-region semantics: (a) aggregates per-tenant and per-tenant_cluster quota and cost counters across regions on a sub-second cadence and propagates throttle flags, plan-change tombstones, cluster-level throttle / suspension flags, key revocations, preservation holds, and erasure tombstones ahead of fine-grained counter replication via a unified fast-path; (b) computes a single canonical-tip view per (chain, fork) by quorum across regional chain pools, excluding votes from pools currently in tip-stale state, and emits coherent rollback notifications keyed on chain coordinates; (c) publishes each tenant's residency policy so edge, tenant_store, usage_meter, and metrics_store enforce it consistently; (d) distributes a hybrid-logical clock used by gateway and fanout in place of wall-clock for ordering and rate-limit bucketing. Gates lifecycle events globally so they cannot collide: cert and origin-endpoint rotations are region-staggered (no two regions transition the same surface in the same maintenance window); chain pool blue/green rotations are gated to one pool / one region / one wave at a time with the canonical-tip quorum size held above its safe threshold throughout; rotation events are tagged so chain_router's schema-skew and tip-divergence quarantines suppress noise during the documented rotation window. Defines and enforces the operator-credential authorization model that backs every operator-override admitted as a CAS proposal anywhere in the system (chain_router pool_membership_manager safe-membership-floor override, tip_quorum operator-override, drain_coordinator force-complete, and any future operator-override surface): each override proposal must carry M-of-N signatures from distinct registered operator credentials (configurable threshold) drawn from a published credential roster; signing operators are recorded with the commit and visible in a per-operator audit trail. Operator credentials are subject to scheduled rotation on a documented cadence; compromise-revocation removes a credential from the roster immediately and invalidates any in-flight override proposals bearing that credential's signature so a compromised credential cannot retroactively or imminently mass-admit attacker-controlled state, with the revocation itself recorded in the audit trail and propagated to local M-of-N gates (chain_router, tip_quorum, drain_coordinator) ahead of further override admission. Exposes an out-of-band cert-bootstrap surface enumerated in cert-inventory for emergency cert recovery: when the inter-region channel cert has effectively expired before in-band rotation could commit and consensus over the channel itself is therefore unavailable, an operator can re-establish channel trust through this surface without requiring consensus over the expired channel; the surface is rooted in an out-of-band trust anchor (offline keys / hardware-rooted root-of-trust) distinct from the inter-region channel cert chain, requires human authorization under the same M-of-N operator-credential model (with a documented elevated threshold for cert re-rooting), and every recovery operation is recorded in the immutable compliance audit trail with operator identity, the cert chain re-rooted, and the HLC of the recovery event. Coordinates tenant offboarding teardown end-to-end: on receipt of an erasure tombstone, signals gateway to close subscriptions, fanout to drop them, address_index to tombstone watch claims, chain_router to cancel in-flight long-RPCs, usage_meter to freeze the cost record, then collects per-component offboarding attestations into the compliance audit trail. Logically a single global service; physically deployed as a quorum across regions so it is not itself a SPOF. Inter-region channel is a cert-bearing surface enumerated in cert-inventory

requirements.description: System exposes Ethereum mainnet on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native JSON-RPC interface
System exposes Sepolia testnet on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native JSON-RPC interface
System exposes Bitcoin on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native JSON-RPC interface
System exposes Cardano on-chain data (current and historical) to authenticated clients via the chain's native interface (Ogmios mini-protocols)
Clients can query state at any historical block on every supported chain (archive semantics, not just recent state)
Clients can subscribe over WebSocket and receive every new block header as it is observed by the corresponding chain node
Clients can subscribe over WebSocket and receive pending/unconfirmed transactions, including Cardano via the Ogmios local-tx-monitor mini-protocol
Clients can subscribe over WebSocket to a watched address and receive an event whenever that address sends or receives value on the corresponding chain
Every request and subscription is authenticated to a specific tenant via an API key looked up in the tenant store
Per-API-key request-rate limits and usage quotas are enforced before the request reaches a chain node
Each chain's native JSON-RPC / mini-protocol surface is exposed to clients without translation to a unified cross-chain schema
The system delivers reorg-safe semantics: WebSocket subscribers receive explicit rollback notifications, and REST/RPC responses can express finality status
For every supported chain, the system maintains multiple healthy chain-node replicas; failure of any single replica does not cause a client-visible error or subscription drop
Every chain-node replica is continuously health-checked; unhealthy replicas are excluded from the routing pool until they recover
Every chain has an explicit finality model and every emitted event carries the chain's confirmation depth and finality status at emission time
When a reorg occurs at any depth, subscribers receive an explicit rollback notification identifying the divergence point and a replay of the new canonical events
Subscribers can configure a per-stream confirmation threshold; events below the threshold are not delivered as confirmed
System supports at least 1M concurrent websocket subscribers per chain stream without per-process bottlenecks
Subscription fanout is decoupled from request handling; new subscribers do not degrade RPC request latency
System maintains a per-chain index of block events keyed by address so address-subscription matching scales sub-linearly in the number of subscribers
System enforces a per-request and per-tenant cost budget on chain queries; over-budget requests are rejected with guidance to chunk or use the historical pool
Long-running historical queries do not contend with tip-state requests on the same chain-node replica
Gateway caches tenant credentials and rate-limit state with explicit TTLs so a transient tenant_store outage does not cause a service outage
When tenant_store is unreachable, gateway operates in a documented degraded mode (cache-served auth, queued counter updates) and surfaces the degradation in metrics
Tenants can rotate API keys without service interruption (multiple active keys per tenant, immediate revocation, hot replacement)
System detects anomalous API-key usage (geo, IP, request-pattern shifts) and alerts the tenant
Pending-transaction events are emitted as transitions in a documented per-chain state machine (seen, replaced-by, dropped, confirmed) so subscribers can reason about non-monotonic mempool changes
Every event on a subscription stream carries an opaque cursor; clients can reconnect and request 'resume from cursor X' to replay missed events within a documented retention window
Untrusted public traffic is filtered at an edge layer (TLS termination, IP rate-limit, WAF, bot mitigation) before it reaches the gateway's chain-bound code paths
Every supported chain has a documented upgrade procedure that pre-stages new node/bridge versions and transitions traffic across forks without a client-visible outage
Every subscription and response surface advertises a protocol/schema version so client code can detect and negotiate compatible behaviour across chain upgrades
System runs active-active in at least two independent regions; failure of any one region does not cause a global outage and clients reconnect into a surviving region without manual intervention
tenant_store state is replicated across regions with bounded lag; each region can authenticate and rate-limit using local replicas
System measures per-tenant cost drivers beyond request count (chain-node CPU, response bytes / egress) and attributes them to the tenant in near-real-time
Each tenant plan has explicit monthly cost ceilings; approaching the ceiling triggers warnings, crossing it triggers throttle/reject with a clear error
Tenants can read per-key usage, error, latency, and rate-limit-headroom metrics for at least the past 30 days through a metrics API
System cross-checks chain head and canonical block hashes across multiple chain-node replicas and quarantines any replica that diverges from the consensus tip
Where a chain has multiple production-quality client implementations, the chain-node pool includes more than one implementation to bound client-bug blast radius
Per chain, the system supports tiered storage (hot recent state, cold deep archive with on-demand re-warming) so storage cost grows sub-linearly with chain history
For tip-state requests, the chain pool can include pruned (non-archive) replicas; tip-state read capacity scales independently of archive storage

Per-tenant quota and cost-ceiling enforcement aggregates counters across all regions on a bounded sub-second cadence so that overshoot is bounded by aggregation latency, not by tenant_store replication lag

When a tenant crosses a global cost or rate ceiling, a throttle flag propagates to every region's auth_cache faster than fine-grained counter replication, so subsequent requests in any region are rejected immediately

Concurrent writes to tenant_store across regions resolve under an explicit, documented conflict-resolution policy (CRDT, partition by tenant home region, or write quorum) so that no key revocation can be 'un-revoked' by a conflicting concurrent write
Key and tenant revocations are stored as tombstones with global ordering so any region's auth_cache hydration sees a revocation regardless of replication lag direction

Subscription cursors are portable across regions: a cursor issued in region A can be resumed from in region B, and the system reconstructs missed events from a globally-meaningful coordinate (chain block + offset or a chain-stream sequence) when the local ring buffer does not cover the requested cursor

For each supported chain, the system advertises a single canonical-tip view across all regions, computed by quorum across regional chain pools, so that the canonical chain history a subscriber sees is independent of which region they connect to

When a reorg is detected, the rollback notification carries a globally-meaningful divergence point (chain coordinate, not region-local cursor) so all regions emit a coherent rollback to their subscribers regardless of when each region's chain pool observes the reorg

Cross-region event ordering exposed to subscribers is derived from chain-native sequencing (block + intra-block index, or chain-stream sequence) rather than gateway wall-clock, so cross-region clients see the same ordering regardless of inter-region clock skew

Rate-limit windows and other time-bucketed enforcement use a hybrid-logical or coordinated clock that bounds inter-region skew explicitly; observed skew above a threshold puts the affected region into a documented degraded mode

Each tenant has an explicit residency policy that constrains the regions in which their tenant data, traffic, and derived telemetry may live; the system enforces this policy at the edge, in tenant_store partitioning, and in metrics_store / usage_meter sharding

Edge routing is residency-aware: requests from a residency-pinned tenant are forwarded only to gateways in regions allowed by that tenant's policy, even when an out-of-policy region is closer by anycast

When connections drop en masse (anycast flap, region drain, edge restart), the system bounds the reconnect-storm load on surviving regions through advertised jittered-backoff hints, bulk auth_cache hydration paths, and pre-warmed fanout state for the most likely failover regions

The internal pub/sub layer that fanout uses to multiplex chain streams is modeled as an explicit component with its own health, capacity, and failover semantics, so its failure modes are visible to operators and to stress testing

fanout exposes a per-subscription consumer-rate feedback signal and accepts batched subscribe calls from gateway, so gateway can implement bounded per-subscription backpressure (slow-consumer overflow policy) and reconnect-storm subscribe-coalescing without saturating fanout's subscribe-RPC fan-out

chain_router returns a per-method cost-class hint at RPC submission time so gateway can partition its in-flight slot pool (short-RPC vs long-RPC pools) and prevent long-tail historical queries from starving short ones

auth_cache stores the per-tenant throttle flag with an explicit version so gateway's long-running paths (active websocket subscriptions, streaming/chunked RPC responses) can re-check the flag cheaply by version comparison without re-running the full auth path

edge consumes a per-region gateway health surface that aggregates per-Subrole liveness (in particular fanout-suspended) so anycast / residency-aware routing can shift subscription traffic away from a region whose subscription path is degraded, even when that region's RPC path is healthy

usage_meter accepts a tagged 'rejected-request' signal from gateway with rejection reason (rate-limit, throttle, residency, revoked, malformed-auth) so per-tenant cost attribution covers shadow load from rejected requests and key-anomaly detection sees the rejection signal

Every TLS / mTLS-bearing surface in the system is enumerated as part of the spec — public edge ingress, gateway↔chain_router, gateway↔fanout, gateway↔auth_cache, gateway↔tenant_store, chain_router↔chain pool, region_coordinator inter-region channel — and each has a documented renewal cadence with an explicit pre-expiry safety margin.
Cert rotation on any surface includes a documented overlap window during which both the outgoing and incoming credential are accepted, so peers that pin or strict-validate do not see a hard cutover.

Region-staggered rotation: region_coordinator gates rotation roll-out across regions so that no two regions can transition the same surface inside the same maintenance window. Simultaneous expiry across regions is prevented by construction, not by deployment discipline.

Gateway and chain_router classify TLS / mTLS handshake failures as a distinct error class from upstream-chain network errors, so on-call signal and tenant-facing error responses point at the correct surface (cert vs chain) instead of conflating them.

Every JSON-RPC response forwarded from a chain pool through chain_router is canonicalized against a per-chain, per-method schema before it reaches gateway: undocumented optional fields are stripped or sorted, types are coerced, and intra-response ordering rules are applied so that response shape is a function of (chain, method, schema_version) and is independent of which client implementation in the pool produced it.

When a chain pool replica produces responses whose canonicalized shape differs from the pool consensus shape for the same (method, schema_version), chain_router quarantines that replica from the active pool the same way it quarantines a divergent-tip replica, and surfaces the skew to operators.

Per-chain response schema_version is part of the protocol-version surface advertised on every response, and is bumped on intentional canonicalization changes so tenants can pin a schema_version and detect drift independently of chain protocol upgrades.

Plan-change events (upgrade, downgrade, suspension) are stored and propagated as globally-ordered tombstones with an effective-from timestamp so any region's auth_cache and tenant_store hydration sees a consistent view of which plan is in force at any point in time, regardless of replication lag direction.

usage_meter tags every cost record with (tenant, plan_version) so that month-to-date cost is attributable to the plan that was in force at the time the cost was incurred. region_coordinator's monthly-ceiling computation aggregates by plan_version, then applies a documented reconciliation policy when plans change mid-period.

When a tenant's resource usage exceeds the new plan's caps at the moment of downgrade (concurrent subscriptions, long-RPC slots, in-flight quota), existing in-flight resources are not torn down; new requests over the new caps are rejected with a 'plan-change overage' reason routed through the rejected-request signal.

chain_router exposes an explicit drain state for chain pool replicas: a draining replica receives no new requests, finishes in-flight RPCs (or returns a retryable-on-other-replica signal to gateway), and only unsubscribes from fanout's head streams after gateway has re-bound the affected subscriptions to a non-draining replica.

region_coordinator gates pool-rotation events globally: at most one pool, one region, one rotation wave at a time, and the canonical-tip quorum size is held above its safe threshold throughout. Rotations are scheduled, not ad-hoc.

Schema-skew quarantine and tip-divergence quarantine both consult a 'rotation in progress' tag from region_coordinator and suppress quarantines triggered solely by the documented rotation window, so rotation noise does not look like a misbehaving replica.

fanout distinguishes a planned head-stream rebind (driven by chain pool rotation) from a network fault, so subscription cursors and consumer-rate state are preserved through the rebind and only a single 'rebind' event surfaces to subscribers (no spurious rollback).

Each chain has an explicit per-chain tip-freshness budget (max acceptable lag from upstream chain tip). chain_router measures pool tip lag against an out-of-band reference (peer-regional pools, chain peer count, expected slot advance) and marks the pool 'tip-stale' when it exceeds the budget.
region_coordinator's canonical-tip quorum excludes votes from any chain pool currently in tip-stale state, so a stalled regional pool cannot anchor the global canonical-tip view.

When gateway answers a tip-state RPC from a tip-stale pool, the response is annotated with the pool's freshness state (lag, last-tip-observed-at) so tenants distinguish 'no new chain activity' from 'we are not seeing new chain activity'.

Head-event and watched-address subscriptions emit a periodic progress heartbeat that includes the pool's last-observed-tip and freshness state, so a silent subscription is distinguishable from a healthy chain quiet period and from a stalled pool.

Pending-transaction / mempool subscription delivery follows a documented fairness model: cross-subscriber delivery order for the same event is deterministic in (event_id, subscription_id), with an explicit upper bound on best-vs-worst delivery skew. Consumer-rate feedback (bubble-gateway-1) is advisory only for mempool streams.

No internal, admin, or co-located subscriber receives mempool events on a faster path than external tenants. fanout's mempool delivery does not privilege any subscriber by network locality, internal status, or commercial agreement; if priority is sold as a product it is a separate documented contract, not an emergent property.

The mempool stream subscription contract surface (advertised to clients via the protocol-version surface) documents the fairness regime, the delivery-skew budget, and the fact that no privileged early access exists.

The system models a tenant_cluster identity that groups tenants by signup metadata, source-network fingerprints, behavioral signals, and query-pattern similarity. Every tenant carries a current cluster id; cluster assignment evolves as more behavioral signal accrues.

Free-tier and trial-tier global quotas are enforced at the tenant_cluster level, not only the per-tenant level. usage_meter aggregates cost and rate by cluster; the throttle-flag fast-path supports cluster-scoped throttle flags that propagate to every region's auth_cache like per-tenant flags do.

Free-tier tenants begin with a low trust score; capacity (concurrent subscriptions, cost class access, mempool stream access, address_index watch counts) unlocks gradually as verified-attribute signals accrue (validated payment instrument, captcha, domain ownership, age-of-tenant, cluster reputation). Trust ramp is documented and inspectable by the tenant.

Cluster-level suspensions (driven by abuse signal) are tombstoned and globally ordered like key revocations, propagate to every region's auth_cache via the same fast-path, and reject all member tenants' new requests with a documented 'cluster-suspended' rejection reason.

Every store holding tenant-attributable data (tenant_store, usage_meter, metrics_store, address_index, auth_cache hydration log) supports a documented 'extract for tenant T' operation returning only T's data, scoped to the residency policy in force, suitable for fulfilling a lawful-access or data-subject-access request without disclosing other tenants.

Every data class held in the system has an explicit retention policy with a documented minimum (regulatory floor) and maximum (privacy ceiling). Retention is enforced as automated rotation, not manual cleanup, and is inspectable per tenant.

Preservation orders are recorded as tombstoned hold records keyed on (tenant, data_class, scope, time_range); held data is exempt from retention rotation. Holds are globally ordered and propagate cross-region. While a hold is in force, erasure of overlapping data is denied with a documented reason.

Tenant erasure requests are durable tombstones that propagate cross-region like revocations. Each store produces a verifiable per-store deletion attestation; the aggregate certificate of deletion is auditable. Erasure-preservation conflicts resolve under a documented preservation-wins policy.

All compliance operations (extract, hold-create, hold-release, erasure-request, erasure-attestation) are logged in an immutable, append-only audit trail that is itself residency-scoped and itself retention-managed. Operator identity is captured per operation.

Every inbound request reaching gateway carries a short-lived, cryptographically signed edge-attestation produced by edge that includes the request's residency tag, source-network classification, and edge-applied rate-limit verdicts. gateway rejects any request without a current valid attestation, regardless of source IP or apparent network position.

Traffic that legitimately bypasses edge (health checks, control plane, region_coordinator → gateway calls) carries a distinct internal-identity attestation, not an implicit network-position trust. Gateway treats absence of attestation as untrusted regardless of source.

Origin endpoints (the IP/hostname pairs gateway accepts on) rotate on a documented cadence under region_coordinator's gating, neutralizing leaked-origin windows; rotation is region-staggered like cert rotation so no two regions rotate simultaneously.

Every chain has an explicit, documented set of supported forks identified by (chain_id, fork_id). chain_router partitions each chain pool by fork allegiance; replicas on different forks belong to different sub-pools and are not treated as divergent under R-chain-cross-check.

region_coordinator maintains a separate canonical-tip per (chain, fork) and reports it as such. Tenants explicitly subscribe to or query a (chain, fork) pair; the protocol-version surface advertises which forks are currently supported.

Detection of an unannounced consensus split (replicas in a pool diverging into two stable subgroups, neither a transient reorg) surfaces a 'fork-detected' alert with a documented operator-decision SLA before the split is exposed to tenants as a separate fork sub-pool.

Tenant offboarding triggers a documented end-to-end teardown coordinated by region_coordinator: open subscriptions closed with a structured reason, fanout state dropped, address_index watches removed, in-flight long-RPCs cancelled, usage_meter cost record frozen at offboarding time. Each component emits an offboarding attestation collected into the compliance audit trail.

Once a tenant is offboarded and the erasure attestation is final, that tenant identity cannot be resurrected. Restoring service to the same human/organization requires a new tenant identity. Attempts to reuse an offboarded tenant id are rejected with a documented reason.

When address_index removes a watch entry for an offboarded tenant on an address that other tenants also watch, only that tenant's claim on the watch is removed; the underlying watch persists for other tenants. Removal is recorded as a per-tenant tombstone, not a hard delete of the watch row.

chain_router must tag every head observation submitted to region_coordinator's tip_quorum with its source replica identity, authenticated via the cert-bearing inter-region surface, so per-source rate limiting and adversarial-source quarantine inside region_coordinator can attribute observations to a specific chain_router replica.

auth_cache must support deny-during-propagation pending markers for the unified fast-path: flag_propagator publishes a pending-marker for high-severity flags (cluster-suspended, key-revocation, erasure-tombstone) before the per-region apply lands, and auth_cache must treat the marker as deny-by-default for the affected identity until the per-region apply commits and a flag-applied attestation is written back.

Residency-policy consumers (edge, gateway, usage_meter, metrics_store) must pin the policy_version they enforced on outgoing requests, propagate it downstream so mismatch is detectable, and acknowledge readiness within the push-and-acknowledge window before residency_publisher activates a tightening change; consumers that fail to acknowledge default to deny-by-default for the affected tenant rather than serve under the old version past activation.

Downstream offboarding components (gateway, fanout, address_index, chain_router, usage_meter) must dedupe offboarding signals by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id) and meet a documented attestation SLO; on timeout, region_coordinator records a best-effort attestation rather than waiting indefinitely, so component teams must surface their actual attestation latency and any preservation-blocked terminal states.

auth_cache must honor pending-marker HLC expiry bounds and originating-proposal-id: a pending-marker auto-clears at the carried HLC expiry without explicit retraction, and auth_cache rejects pending-markers lacking an originating-proposal-id, so a stalled or rejected proposal cannot indefinitely deny traffic via a stuck pending-marker.

An out-of-band cert-bootstrap surface must exist at parent scope so that, in the emergency-cert-recovery state where the inter-region channel cert has effectively expired before in-band rotation could commit, an operator can re-establish channel trust without requiring consensus over the channel itself.

lifecycle_gate's operator-override admission path for chain_router pool_membership_manager (emergency-rollover replica admission that bypasses safe-membership-floor) needs the same parent-scope operator-credential authorization model with M-of-N signing requirements, credential-rotation, compromise-revocation, and per-operator audit so a single compromised credential cannot mass-admit attacker-controlled replicas; chain_router enforces local M-of-N gating for the override but parent scope must define and enforce the operator credential model that backs both tip_quorum and chain_router overrides.

satisfactions.explanation: eth_archive is an Ethereum mainnet archive node serving the chain's native JSON-RPC; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to it
sepolia_archive is a Sepolia testnet archive node serving the chain's native JSON-RPC; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to it
btc_archive is a Bitcoin Core full node with txindex; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to its JSON-RPC and notification interface
ada_archive is a Cardano node + Ogmios bridge exposing chain-sync, local-state-query, and local-tx-monitor; the gateway proxies authenticated requests to it
All four chain nodes are configured in archive mode (or with full history), so historical state at any block is reachable through their native interfaces
The gateway opens a long-lived chain-sync / newHeads subscription against each chain node and forwards new headers to subscribed websocket clients
The gateway subscribes to each chain node's pending-transaction stream (eth newPendingTransactions, btc ZMQ rawmempool, ada Ogmios local-tx-monitor) and forwards pending txs to subscribed clients
The gateway evaluates each new block and pending-tx event against client-supplied address filters and pushes a match event to the relevant subscribers
The gateway resolves the API key on every connection/request against tenant_store and tags the session with the tenant identity
The gateway updates per-key rate-limit and quota counters in tenant_store on each request and rejects requests that exceed the tenant's configured limits
The gateway forwards JSON-RPC method calls verbatim per chain (eth_*, btc getblock/getrawtransaction/etc., Ogmios mini-protocols) without rewriting them into a common schema

The gateway tracks rollback events emitted by each chain node's chain-sync/newHeads stream and forwards them as explicit rollback messages on the matching websocket subscriptions; REST responses include the chain head's finality at request time

Each chain pool (eth_archive, sepolia_archive, btc_archive, ada_archive) is now defined as a managed group of replicas; chain_router selects from healthy replicas, so single-replica failure is invisible to clients
chain_router's replica-selection policy continuously health-checks pool members and excludes unhealthy ones until they recover
fanout tags every emitted event with the source chain's confirmation depth and finality status before delivery
fanout subscribes to chain pools' chain-sync streams, observes rollbacks, and emits explicit rollback notifications + canonical replay through its multiplex layer
Subscriptions accepted by the gateway carry a confirmation-threshold parameter; fanout filters events below the threshold per stream
The dedicated fanout service is horizontally scalable; a single chain stream is consumed once and multiplexed via internal pub/sub to many subscriber-handling fanout instances
Subscription state lives in the fanout service, not the gateway, so RPC request handling on the gateway is unaffected by subscriber count
fanout populates address_index keyed by address as it processes each block; address-activity subscribers register at the index and only receive matched events
chain_router enforces per-tenant query-cost budgets (request and monthly), rejecting or chunking over-budget requests with explicit guidance
chain_router routes long-running historical queries to the archive subset of each chain pool, separated from the pruned-tip subset that serves tip-state requests
auth_cache (a gateway-local Store) holds tenant credentials and rate-limit state with explicit TTLs, populated from tenant_store and consulted on every authenticated request

When tenant_store is unreachable on cache miss, gateway operates in a degraded mode using the existing auth_cache entries; usage_meter queues counter updates for replay; degradation surfaces as a metric
tenant_store models multiple active keys per tenant with revocation timestamps; gateway/auth_cache honour revocation immediately on TTL refresh
usage_meter tracks per-key behavioural baselines (geo, IP, request pattern) and flags anomalies into metrics_store and tenant alerts
fanout normalises each chain's mempool semantics into a documented pending-tx state machine (seen / replaced-by / dropped / confirmed) and emits state-transition events
fanout assigns an opaque cursor to every emitted event and retains a per-chain ring buffer; clients reconnecting can request 'resume from cursor X' within the documented retention window
edge service terminates TLS, applies IP rate-limiting, runs WAF + bot-mitigation rules, and only forwards API-key-bearing traffic to the gateway

Each chain pool's definition allows replica replacement; pre-fork upgrade pre-stages new replicas in the pool, gradually shifts traffic via chain_router/fanout, and retires old versions after the fork window
gateway, chain_router, and fanout advertise a protocol/schema version on every subscription handshake and RPC response so client code can detect breaking changes

edge anycasts traffic across regions; gateway, chain_router, fanout, auth_cache, address_index, usage_meter, and metrics_store are deployed per region; clients reconnect into a surviving region transparently
tenant_store is now defined as multi-region replicated, with each region holding a local replica readable by gateway and usage_meter
usage_meter receives per-request signals from gateway and chain_router (request count, chain-node CPU estimate, response bytes, websocket egress) and attributes them per tenant in near-real-time
usage_meter enforces monthly per-tenant cost ceilings; approaching the ceiling emits warnings, crossing it triggers throttle/reject decisions enforced by gateway and chain_router via auth_cache flags

usage_meter writes per-tenant usage, error, latency, and rate-limit-headroom metrics to metrics_store with at least 30 days of retention; the gateway exposes a metrics API that reads from metrics_store
chain_router cross-checks chain heads and canonical block hashes across multiple replicas in each pool, quarantining divergent replicas via the same health-check path
Each chain pool's definition explicitly admits multiple client implementations (e.g. Erigon + Geth for Ethereum) to bound client-bug blast radius
Each chain pool's definition includes both archive replicas (cold deep history) and pruned replicas (hot recent state); chain_router routes queries to the appropriate tier
Each chain pool's definition explicitly includes pruned tip-only replicas; chain_router routes tip-state requests to them, scaling tip-read capacity independently of archive storage

usage_meter reports per-tenant deltas to region_coordinator on a sub-second cadence; region_coordinator aggregates them globally and bounds overshoot to aggregation latency rather than tenant_store replication lag

region_coordinator writes_to auth_cache: when any region's aggregated counter crosses a global ceiling, region_coordinator pushes a throttle flag into every region's auth_cache, propagating ahead of fine-grained counter replication

tenant_store is redefined with per-key single-writer in the tenant's home region for adds/updates plus globally-tombstoned revocations, so concurrent writes resolve under an explicit policy that cannot un-revoke a key
tenant_store tombstones revocations globally and any region's auth_cache hydration sees the tombstone regardless of replication direction

fanout's redefinition tags every event with a globally-meaningful chain coordinate alongside the opaque cursor; replay can be served from any region by reconstructing from the chain pool's history when its local ring buffer doesn't cover the requested coordinate

region_coordinator computes a single per-chain canonical-tip view by quorum across regional chain pools (chain_router calls region_coordinator with head observations); fanout and chain_router consult region_coordinator for the canonical tip

region_coordinator emits rollback notifications keyed on globally-meaningful chain coordinates; fanout in every region forwards the same coherent rollback regardless of when its local chain pool observed the reorg
fanout's redefinition specifies that subscriber-visible ordering uses chain-derived sequencing (block + intra-block index, or chain-stream sequence), not gateway wall-clock

gateway uses the hybrid logical clock distributed by region_coordinator for time-bucketed enforcement; gateway's redefinition specifies a degraded mode when observed inter-region skew crosses a threshold

chain_router 'detects unannounced consensus splits (replicas in a pool diverging into two stable subgroups, neither a transient reorg) and emits a fork-detected alert with a documented operator-decision SLA before the split becomes user-visible'

region_coordinator 'coordinates tenant offboarding teardown end-to-end: signals gateway to close subscriptions, fanout to drop them, address_index to tombstone watch claims, chain_router to cancel in-flight long-RPCs, usage_meter to freeze the cost record, then collects per-component offboarding attestations into the compliance audit trail'
tenant_store 'once a tenant is offboarded and its erasure attestation is final, that tenant identity cannot be resurrected — attempts to reuse the id are rejected'

address_index 'when a tenant offboards, only that tenant's claim on a watched address is removed (recorded as a per-tenant tombstone), never a hard delete of the underlying watch row when other tenants share it'

chain_router definition now states: 'Every head observation submitted to region_coordinator's tip_quorum is tagged with the authenticated source replica identity of the submitting chain_router replica, signed over the cert-bearing inter-region surface (mTLS to region_coordinator), so region_coordinator's tip_quorum can attribute each observation to a specific chain_router replica and apply per-source rate limiting and adversarial-source quarantine.'

auth_cache definition now states: 'Supports deny-during-propagation pending markers on the unified fast-path: when flag_propagator publishes a pending-marker for a high-severity flag (cluster-suspended, key-revocation, erasure-tombstone) before the per-region apply lands, auth_cache treats the pending-marker as deny-by-default for the affected identity until the per-region apply commits and a flag-applied attestation is written back to flag_propagator.'

edge, gateway, usage_meter, metrics_store definitions all now pin and propagate the residency policy_version, subscribe to region_coordinator's residency_publisher push-and-acknowledge channel, must acknowledge readiness within the documented window before tightening activation, and 'fall to deny-by-default for the affected tenant rather than serve under the old version past activation' if not acknowledged.

gateway, fanout, address_index, chain_router, usage_meter definitions all now state they 'dedupe inbound offboarding signals from region_coordinator by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meet a documented attestation SLO, and surface preservation-blocked terminal states' so region_coordinator can record a best-effort attestation on timeout.

auth_cache redefinition now states: 'Every accepted pending-marker must carry an originating-proposal-id and an HLC expiry bound; auth_cache rejects pending-markers that lack an originating-proposal-id... Pending-markers auto-clear when their carried HLC expiry bound is reached without an explicit retraction, so a stalled or rejected proposal cannot leave a stuck deny-by-default state in place; on apply commit, auth_cache reconciles the pending-marker by matching the inbound flag-applied attestation's originating-proposal-id to the installed marker rather than by identity alone'

region_coordinator redefinition now states: 'Exposes an out-of-band cert-bootstrap surface enumerated in cert-inventory for emergency cert recovery: when the inter-region channel cert has effectively expired before in-band rotation could commit and consensus over the channel itself is therefore unavailable, an operator can re-establish channel trust through this surface without requiring consensus over the expired channel; the surface is rooted in an out-of-band trust anchor (offline keys / hardware-rooted root-of-trust) distinct from the inter-region channel cert chain, requires human authorization under the same M-of-N operator-credential model (with a documented elevated threshold for cert re-rooting), and every recovery operation is recorded in the immutable compliance audit trail'

region_coordinator now defines and enforces the operator-credential authorization model that backs every operator-override admitted as a CAS proposal anywhere in the system (chain_router pool_membership_manager safe-membership-floor override, tip_quorum operator-override...): M-of-N signatures from distinct registered operator credentials drawn from a published credential roster, scheduled rotation, compromise-revocation that immediately removes the credential and invalidates any in-flight override proposals bearing it, and per-operator audit trail. chain_router redefinition states: 'Every operator-override admission path inside chain_router... is gated locally and admitted only when the override proposal carries M-of-N signatures from distinct operator credentials drawn from region_coordinator's published credential roster... refuses to commit override proposals after a compromise-revocation has invalidated any in-flight signature, records the signing operator identities with each commit'. Single redefinition pair satisfies both the chain_router pool-admit override and tip_quorum override credential model
